decisions.executionNote: Raise and turn the left wrist toward an elbow-up, downward approach to the mallet handle; right arm remains parked.
Continue rotating down while translating above the near end of the handle; maintain elbow-up continuity.
Align fingers transverse to the handle and lower carefully toward a grasp near its free end.
Use the wrist view to center the shaft between the jaws and adjust the grasp slightly inward from its end.
Correct the handle's slight yaw and lateral offset, then close the left gripper around the shaft.
Finish closing, then lift the handle vertically to verify visually that the mallet is retained.
Mallet is visibly retained. Move its head above the leftmost red key, keeping the left wrist in its own workspace and the mallet elevated.
Lower the retained mallet vertically onto the first red key; inspect tip alignment and contact before moving to the next key.
Complete the first key's downward stroke, then lift 5 cm clear before any lateral advance.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Advance above the orange key then strike vertically, leaving the right arm still.
Lift 6 cm after the orange-key stroke, then move above the third, yellow key without dragging across the bars.
Strike the third yellow key vertically, then lift the retained mallet over 6 cm before proceeding.
Advance the elevated mallet to the fourth green bar, then make a vertical strike while keeping the left wrist left of center.
Lift 6 cm after the green-bar strike, then advance to the fifth cyan bar with the mallet clear of the keys.
Strike the fifth cyan key and lift 6.5 cm afterward, retaining the mallet and leaving the other arm parked.
Advance clear of the keys to the sixth blue bar and strike downward without lateral dragging.
Lift 6 cm after the sixth blue key, then position above the seventh purple bar while preserving the grasp.
Strike the seventh purple key vertically, then lift 6.5 cm before advancing to the final key.
Advance the lifted mallet to the final magenta key and strike vertically; keep the left wrist in the left workspace.
